design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. A household rings to close off a folio and pay what is owed. The folio they are looking at is three charges short of the truth, and none of the three is anything the caller mentions: the resort charge was posted for only two of the nights the party was in the unit, nothing at all has been posted for servicing the unit, for the dog or for the parking space beyond the one included, and the nights the party gave up by driving home early have never been retained. The settlement terms say outright that the amount collected waits on all three, so the agent must read the terms, look at the folio, see what is missing, work each of the three out on its own multi-factor basis and post it, and only then work out what is actually collected today. Every one of the four figures turns on records that have to be read rather than assumed: an occupancy file that is a night short of the recorded departure, resort entries covering part of the stay, a date change request that stands accepted and another that stands withdrawn, a claim that stands under assessment rather than allowed, credit sitting on a pass standing active and on one standing cancelled, a dining balance smaller than the dining charges. An agent who reads only the four computation documents and none of the factor documents posts 72.00, 304.00, 2116.00 and 3597.01, and every one of those is wrong.

SCOPE (Principle C). Occupied by task 0: lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting and lodging_ext_reservation_deposit, with post_stay_room_charge_ee3504ba and authorise_reservation_deposit_3e63cb2f — the pricing of a stay onto its folio before arrival and the deposit asked for. Claimed here: lodging_ext_stay_resort_charge, lodging_ext_departure_service_charge, lodging_ext_early_departure_charge and lodging_ext_departure_settlement, with post_stay_resort_charge_f79fa34a, post_departure_service_charge_1468621e, post_early_departure_charge_bb461064 and settle_departure_folio_07fd1088 — everything on the far side of the stay. The two scopes are disjoint in policies and in tools, and between them they cover all six extended policies of this difficulty, which is the whole set. No policy, route or tool is held back for a later task: this is the last of the two.

STEP 0 DRAW, as printed by scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/lodging_reservations_desk --task 1:
{"task": 1, "key": "ski_resort_operator/lodging_reservations_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 5]}
The tree is the root plus exactly three prerequisite problems, and the four computations carry 6, 4, 4 and 5 declared factors. The retained room rate took the 6, the resort charge and the settlement took the two 4s, and the departure services charge took the 5; the multiset matches the draw. With three prerequisite problems at least two edges must be value_input; all three are.

POLICIES, LINEAGE AND TRIGGERS. All four are state_due: with no customer ringing at all, a departed stay whose resort charge, servicing and retained nights are not on its folio is money the collective should have on its books at month end, and a folio still showing an amount to be collected is money it should have collected.
lodging_ext_stay_resort_charge: base_policy_refs [lodging_rate_and_fees, lodging_agg_household_stay_pricing]. One overwrite, declared: base's sentence that the nightly resort charge is posted for every night occupied and is not reduced by any discount is superseded by the sentence that posts it as one entry over the nights the folio shows occupied, since the member tier does reduce it. Base's gate on the state a resort charge may be posted in is inherited and carried into solvability_contract.
lodging_ext_departure_service_charge: base_policy_refs [lodging_stay_operations, lodging_rate_and_fees]. One overwrite, declared: base's "The housekeeping charge is posted once on departure and the parking charge nightly for spaces beyond those included." is named verbatim and replaced by the sentence that makes those two published figures the starting point and varies each of them by the records, with a turnover charge added on top of the housekeeping charge. Base fixes both figures as that policy's own per-tier parameters, so the ladders are an override and are declared as one rather than described as new ground. The in-room dining service share is genuinely new ground — no base sentence fixes a service charge on folio incidentals — and is added rather than substituted.
lodging_ext_early_departure_charge: base_policy_refs [lodging_modification, lodging_rate_and_fees, lodging_cancellation]; lodging_modification governs the subject lodging_fee_charge and its state gate is inherited. Two overwrites, declared: base's "A night the party leaves early is still charged where the departure falls inside the cancellation terms of the stay." is replaced by the sentence that works the retention out on the nights given up; and base's "After the deadline the unit type's late cancellation nights of room rate are retained, worked out at the rate of the first nights of the stay, and the remainder comes back." is replaced by the sentence pricing the retained nights at the nightly average of the room rate standing on the folio. The notice period this policy counts back from the departure date is its own declared constant, the early departure notice period, and not base's change notice period counted back from the arrival date, so base's change deadline is left exactly as it stands. The rule states in terms that a party leaving early has not changed the reservation, so base's change fee does not arise.
lodging_ext_departure_settlement: base_policy_refs [lodging_checkout_settlement]. Two overwrites, declared: base's order of deposit, then credit, then the payment method is replaced by the fixed order of four; and base's "The folio is presented on departure and settled before the party leaves the mountain." is replaced by the sentence settling a folio the household takes up later on the same basis. Base's other sentences, including the states in which a deposit may be applied and the release period for the incidental hold, are inherited untouched and bind the application of a deposit rather than this collection.

FACTOR CARD — lodging_ext_stay_resort_charge (4 declared), gold 42.00.
1 charged_nights_basis (method): nights from arrival to a recorded departure where the occupancy file is short / every night the reservation covers where no departure is recorded / the nights the folio shows consumed. Tier taken: the first, on the three night_consume entries against the recorded departure of 2026-12-30. Baseline: the folio's three nights, giving 21.00.
2 member_resort_nightly (parameter, cross-difficulty on passes, multi-source): both an active pass and an active dining plan / one of them / neither. Tier taken: the first. Baseline: the unit type's 24.00, giving 60.00.
3 nights_already_charged_offset (parameter, folio history): entries covering some of the nights / entries covering all of them / no entry. Tier taken: the first, on the two resort entries of one night each. Baseline: every night charged, giving 84.00.
4 holiday_window_supplement (parameter, date span): every night the reservation covers inside the holiday window / some of them / none. Tier taken: the first. Baseline: nothing added, giving 33.60. The rule now judges the supplement over the nights the reservation covers, which is what the compute counts.
Whole-baseline fall-back: 72.00, against gold 42.00.

FACTOR CARD — lodging_ext_departure_service_charge (5 declared), gold 450.59.
1 service_night_basis (method): every night the reservation covers / the nights to a recorded departure / the nights the folio shows consumed. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: the folio's three, giving 384.59.
2 servicing_state_charge (parameter, multi-source): a dog and a long stay / one of the two / neither. Tier taken: the second, one dog with three nights occupied against a threshold of five. Baseline: the 85.00 charge as it stands, giving 429.34.
3 passholder_parking_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty on passes, multi-source): spaces beyond those included with an active pass / no spaces beyond / otherwise. Tier taken: the first. Baseline: the unit type's 28.00, giving 478.59.
4 in_room_dining_service_share (parameter, cross-difficulty on dining, multi-source): in-room dining charges with an active plan / without one / no such charge. Tier taken: the first, on 244.50 of in-room dining. Baseline: nothing added, giving 421.25.
5 occupancy_turnover_charge (parameter, multi-source): a party filling the maximum occupancy / a party beyond the standard occupancy / neither. Tier taken: the first. Baseline: nothing added, giving 399.59.
Whole-baseline fall-back: 304.00, against gold 450.59.

FACTOR CARD — lodging_ext_early_departure_charge (6 declared), gold 630.12.
1 nights_given_up_basis (method): a recorded departure with a short occupancy file / a recorded departure with a complete one / no recorded departure. Tier taken: the first, giving three nights given up. Baseline: what the computation document states for a reservation with a departure recorded — the nights the reservation covers less the nights the folio shows consumed, four — giving 927.69. The baseline is the branch of the document that this world actually reaches, not the no-departure branch.
2 notice_retained_nights (parameter, requests and dates): a request accepted more than the early departure notice period before the departure date / within it / none. Tier taken: the second, on the request of 2026-12-29 against a departure date of 2027-01-02 and a notice period of seven days, so the notice earns the unit type's late cancellation allowance of one night and two of the three given up are retained. Baseline: every night given up, giving 927.69. Near-miss: the withdrawn request of 2026-11-20, which would put the household on the no-night tier.
3 retained_nightly_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty on passes, multi-source): an active pass with the room rate on the folio / an active pass without it / no active pass. Tier taken: the first, 476.10 a night. Baseline: the published holiday rate of 529.00, giving 696.25. Labelled parameter because all three tiers yield one nightly rate multiplied into the same expression; no algorithm changes between them.
4 window_retention_supplement (parameter, date span): every night inside the holiday window / every night inside the peak window / otherwise. Tier taken: the first. Baseline: nothing added, giving 511.10.
5 occupancy_retention (parameter, folio history, multi-source): an occupancy charge on the folio with the retained nights within the late cancellation nights / beyond them / no occupancy charge. Tier taken: the second, two retained nights against one late cancellation night. Baseline: nothing retained, giving 595.12.
6 protection_claim_retention (parameter, cross-difficulty on insure, multi-source): a claim standing allowed / a claim standing under assessment / neither. Tier taken: the second. Baseline: the whole amount charged, giving 1260.25. Labelled parameter, not method: its tiers substitute a share into one unchanged expression rather than changing how the quantity is computed. The computation's method factor is nights_given_up_basis, whose tiers select three different counting rules.
Whole-baseline fall-back: 2116.00 — four nights given up at the published holiday nightly rate of 529.00, which is exactly what the computation document alone yields on this world — against gold 630.12.

FACTOR CARD — lodging_ext_departure_settlement (4 declared), gold 1953.83.
1 disputed_charges_held_back (parameter, requests and folio history): a dispute accepted with an occupancy charge standing / with none / no dispute. Tier taken: the first, holding back the 280.00 occupancy charge. Baseline: nothing held back, giving 2233.83.
2 dining_plan_met_charges (parameter, cross-difficulty on dining, multi-source): an active plan whose balance reaches the dining charges / falls short of them / no plan. Tier taken: the second, 180.00 loaded against 244.50 of dining. Baseline: nothing met, giving 2133.83.
3 deposit_set_against_folio (parameter, folio history): a deposit reaching what is left / falling short of it / no deposit. Tier taken: the second, 833.18 against 3137.01. Baseline: nothing set against it, giving 2787.01.
4 resort_credit_draw (method, cross-difficulty on passes): credit on both a pass record standing active and a ticket order standing in use / on the pass record only / on the ticket order only / neither. Tier taken: the first, 150.00 then 200.00. Baseline: no credit drawn, giving 2303.83. Near-miss: the 400.00 standing on the cancelled pass, which the rule now excludes in terms by naming the state each record must stand in.
Whole-baseline fall-back: 3597.01, against gold 1953.83.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Four exact write subjects, each with its own governing lineage.
Subject lodging_resort_fee is governed by lodging_rate_and_fees, whose gate resort_fee_stay_state applies: condition verbatim "The resort charge is posted only while the reservation stands in the checked_in or checked_out state." The reservation stands checked_out at frozen_time and no gold write moves it. lodging_agg_household_stay_pricing does not govern this subject and is therefore not a base precondition of this write. No time gate.
Subject lodging_incidental_charge is governed by lodging_stay_operations, whose only gate, nights_load_state, binds the loading of the block of nights and not the posting of an incidental charge; it enters as policy_scope. No time gate.
Subject lodging_fee_charge is governed by lodging_modification, whose gate fee_bearing_reservation_state applies: condition verbatim "A fee is posted to a folio only while the reservation stands in the deposit_pending, confirmed, checked_in, checked_out, cancelled or no_show state." The reservation stands checked_out, which is in the allowed set. Its other gate, change_notice_deadline, binds the recording of a change to the reservation and is untouched by this policy, which counts its own early departure notice period back from the departure date and states that an early departure is not a change; so no time gate arises on this write and temporal_feasibility is empty.
Subject lodging_payment is governed by lodging_checkout_settlement, whose two gates both bind the application or return of a deposit rather than the collection of a payment; the policy enters as policy_scope. Note for the audit: no deposit is applied or returned in this task, precisely because that write would carry the release-period time gate; the deposit is set against what is collected as an input of the settlement figure, and the deposit standing on the reservation is left for the closing write this task does not make.
Every gate that does apply correlates to the action by lodging_holdings.lodging_id, which is the parameter each of the four tools takes.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is one reservation: the Slopeside Studio at Granite Ridge for 2026-12-26 to 2027-01-02, lodging_holdings row 23b25877-1a18-4a4a-bda9-c16d6c93717c. The correlation key is lodging_id and every folio entry and every service request carries it. Rows included: the three night_consume entries (the nights basis), the four room rate entries and the occupancy charge (the nightly average, the occupancy retention and the held-back charge), the two resort entries (the offset), the two in-room dining entries (the service share), the spa and retail entries and the payment (what is still to be collected), the deposit entry (what is set against it), and the two requests standing accepted. Rows excluded and why: the request of 2026-11-20 stands withdrawn, so it is neither the notice that limits the retained nights nor a dispute; the cancelled Granite Ridge Local Pass carries 400.00 of credit but is not a record standing active, which the credit ladder now names in terms; the spa and retail charges are incidentals but not dining ones, so the dining plan does not meet them. Nothing on this account has been reversed or compensated. Each of the four tools writes the reservation reference onto the row it creates.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The reservation carries every tier parameter through its unit type, the dates and the recorded departure that three separate night bases rest on, the party and the dog that the servicing, turnover and occupancy elements rest on, and the balances the settlement starts from. The three night_consume entries are one night short of the recorded departure on purpose: delete one and the resort charge, the service charge and the retained nights all move; make them four and three of the four factors that read them fall to their fall-through. The four room rate entries give the nightly average the retained nights are priced at, and the occupancy charge is both the charge held back and the evidence the occupancy element is retained at all. The two resort entries are the offset: without them the resort charge doubles. The two in-room dining entries are the service share; the spa and retail entries are the near-miss for it and for the dining plan. The payment of 500.00 is what makes the folio balance what it is. The deposit entry of 833.18 is what is set against the settlement. The date change request standing accepted is what cuts the retained nights from three to two; the withdrawn one is the trap that would take them to none; the folio dispute is what holds the occupancy charge back. The active pass carries the parking tier, the retained rate tier, the resort member tier and 150.00 of credit; the cancelled pass carries 400.00 of credit that must not be drawn. The ticket order carries the second credit pot; the dining plan carries the member service share, the resort member tier and the 180.00 that meets part of the dining charges; the protection plan carries the claim standing under assessment that halves the retention. Automatic clauses checked: the folio is not closed and closure would require both balances at zero, which they are not; the incidental hold release period runs in business days from 2026-12-30 and is not a gate on any write made here; the balance due date before arrival is long past and the stay has been taken; the reservation is not moved out of checked_out by any of the four writes. No cache field is in play — folio_balance_usd of 2474.30 is exactly the charges less the payment beneath it, and deposit_held_usd of 833.18 is exactly its one deposit entry.

PERSONA DESIGN. Renata is written tired rather than cross, apologetic, in long sentences — a different voice from task 0's brisk errand-runner, and the information comes out in a different order and pace. Volunteered at the opening: that she wants the folio closed off and paid today, and her mobile number. Given only when asked: date of birth, passholder number, postal code, email, who the booking was in, who was in the unit and the dog, and why the stay ended early. Mentioned once without pressing: that she rang yesterday about a charge she did not understand and was told someone would look at it, which is the folio dispute already standing on the record. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: the payment route when payment comes up, running the settlement once it is handed over, and closing when she hears the folio is settled. She states no figure at any point and accepts whatever she is told, so an agent who hands her 3597.01 hears exactly what an agent who hands her 1953.83 hears.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: lodging_ext_departure_settlement, the settlement the caller rang about. Three prerequisite problems, matching the draw, all hanging in parallel off the root, all value_input on the same compute binding, outstanding.
Edge 1, to lodging_ext_early_departure_charge. Prerequisite sentence, in the settlement policy's own rule: "The amount collected at departure is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate retained for the nights of the stay the party gave up." Four-point test: the connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result to what it waits on; the side it waits on is a record-visible state, a retained room rate standing on the folio, in the words the folio uses; it names no tool, no policy id, no code token; and it is written at exactly the strength of the edge. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about.
Edge 2, to lodging_ext_departure_service_charge. Sentence: "It is worked out only once the folio carries the departure services charge the stay owes for servicing the unit and for its nightly extras." Connective "only once"; the state is a departure services charge standing on the folio; no code names; exact scope. One write brings it about.
Edge 3, to lodging_ext_stay_resort_charge. Sentence: "Before it is worked out, the folio must carry the resort charge owed for the nights of the stay." Connective "Before"; the state is a resort charge covering the nights of the stay; no code names; exact scope. One write brings it about.
Derivation for each: the sentence says what the settlement waits on; the folio read shows the state does not hold — no fee entry at all, no housekeeping entry, resort entries for two nights of four; the depended-on policy's own rule says what that charge is and that it is posted to the folio; so the action to take first is to post it, and only then to settle.
Seed evidence that each is unmet at frozen_time is recorded edge by edge in prerequisite_closure.edges[].unresolved_at_frozen_time, down to the row and the field. Topological order: the three charges in any order, then the settlement. Parallel edges: proved commutative in order_uniqueness by a run, with the folio balance figure taken from the harness. Deletion sensitivity, recomputed by the harness rather than asserted: skipping the resort charge takes the settlement from 1953.83 to 1911.83, skipping the services charge to 1503.24, skipping the retention to 1323.71. The customer's own write in this tree is the root, settle_departure_folio_07fd1088, owner user.

LENGTH AND BREADTH. Depth: surface goal (close the folio and pay) -> the settlement terms name three states the figure waits on -> the folio read shows all three missing or short -> the three pricing policies say what each is worth -> post them -> settle on the world they leave. Breadth at each hop: the resort charge reads the occupancy file, the recorded departure, two other product lines and a date window; the services charge reads the same file, the party, the dog, the parking, the in-room dining entries and two product lines; the retention reads the requests, the room rate entries, the occupancy charge, a pass and a claim; the settlement reads every room rate, resort, incidental and fee charge on the folio, a dispute, a dining balance, a deposit and two credit pots.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG. Taking the occupancy file at face value and charging three nights instead of four. Charging the resort charge for all four nights and ignoring the two already posted. Reading the withdrawn date change request instead of the accepted one, which would retain no night at all. Retaining all three nights given up instead of the two the notice leaves. Pricing the retained nights at the published 529.00 instead of the 476.10 the household actually pays. Treating the claim as allowed rather than under assessment, which would charge nothing. Drawing the 400.00 of credit on the cancelled pass. Letting the dining plan meet the spa and retail charges as well. Settling before the three charges are posted, which leaves 2474.30 collected and three entries missing. Every one of these is excluded by a sentence of the published terms read against the records.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by mobile; verify with two details. Read the reservation, the folio, the requests, the passes, the dining plan, the protection plan and the ticket order. Resort charge: four nights owed, two already charged, member nightly 16.80 plus the holiday share 4.20, over two nights = 42.00, posted over two nights. Departure services: 106.25 housekeeping, 180.00 dog, 84.00 parking, 29.34 in-room dining service, 51.00 turnover = 450.59, posted over four nights. Retained room rate: three nights given up, two retained after the notice allowance, at 476.10 with the holiday retention share = 1190.25, plus 70.00 occupancy for the late cancellation night, halved for the open claim = 630.12, posted over two nights. Settlement: 4097.01 charged less 500.00 paid = 3597.01; less 280.00 held back, less 180.00 met by the dining plan, less the 833.18 deposit, less 350.00 of credit = 1953.83, taken from the card on file by the household itself.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The task is built by a script that evaluates each policy's compute with the gate's own evaluator (build_env, eval_compute, substitute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py) on the handling-time world — initial_state with every earlier gold write replayed through the real tools — so every declared expected value, every per-factor baseline, every whole-baseline figure and every skipped-edge counterfactual is the machine's output. Its printed output: resort charge 42.0 (baseline 72.0), departure services 450.59 (baseline 304.0), retained room rate 630.12 (baseline 2116.0), settlement 1953.83 (baseline 3597.01); skipped-edge settlements 1911.83, 1503.24 and 1323.71; folio 3597.01 before the settlement and 1643.18 after it.

CLOSURE. Four policies, four tools, four computations, four write calls, in the topological order of the tree; charter_scope, required_documents and computations.policy_id name exactly those four; charter_scope.task_tools names exactly those four tools in first-call order. Terminal state: the folio carries a resort entry of 42.00 over two nights, a housekeeping entry of 450.59 over four, a cancellation fee entry of 630.12 over two and a payment of 1953.83, and the reservation's folio balance stands at 1643.18 — the 280.00 held back for the duty manager, the 180.00 the dining plan meets, the 350.00 of credit drawn and the 833.18 deposit still standing against it, which is exactly the state the charter says a folio is left in when part of it is with the duty manager and the deposit has not yet been applied. No fifth write and no idle policy.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and only the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the DB the finders return and the caller's own lines: the caller wants the folio closed; the settlement terms name three things the figure waits on; the folio shows a resort charge for two nights of four, no housekeeping entry and no retention; the three pricing documents and their factor documents give 42.00, 450.59 and 630.12 on these records; the settlement terms then give 1953.83 from the card the caller names. The redraft reaches the same four writes, the three charges in any order and the settlement last, with the same arguments.

MANUAL VALUES GATES, COMPLETED AFTER THE SCRIPTS PASSED.
Length, breadth and the hidden test: the four hops were walked from the surface goal to the settlement figure and are set out above; skipping any one of the three prerequisites moves the settlement (1911.83, 1503.24, 1323.71 against 1953.83) and every one of the nineteen declared factors moves a figure when its baseline is substituted. The customer's own write is the settlement.
Expression of the need and the simulator's boundary: the caller names the object, the timing, the authorisation and the mode. She never reads policy, never names a missing charge, never corrects a figure and runs the settlement only after the agent has unlocked and handed it over.
Chronology of the opening world: everything she volunteers points at initial_state rows. She anticipates none of the four figures gold creates and says outright she cannot work the total out.
Base eligibility and the time anchor: checked verbatim; the two state gates hold on the official row, and no time gate binds any of the four subjects, which is why temporal_feasibility is empty.
Authoritative facts and the business object: the claim decision, the request outcomes, the credit balances and the dining balance are all read from the records rather than from the caller. Every folio row entering an aggregate carries this reservation's reference; the withdrawn request and the cancelled pass are excluded by their own recorded state, each named in a rule sentence.
Reachability and no real-world waits: all four figures are computable from records already held; the four writes land synchronously under one frozen_time; nothing waits on the claim being settled, on the duty manager, on a clearing or on a future date.
Prerequisite sentences: the four-point test is set out per edge; all three use the state form and each waits on a state exactly one write of this difficulty brings about.
Two-way equivalence of rule and compute: every binding quotes a rule sentence verbatim (checked mechanically over compute_basis for all four policies), every ladder is stated tier by tier, and the two places where the compute was narrower than the prose — the credit pots' states and the settlement's charge families — are now stated in the rule in the same words the compute uses.
Factors bear weight, the labels are honest, the baseline is honest: each factor's baseline is the branch of its policy's baseline paragraph that this world actually reaches; the three method factors change how a quantity is computed (which nights a charge is worked out over, twice; how the nights given up are counted; which credit pot is drawn and in what order) rather than swapping a number, and the claim share, which only substitutes a multiplier, is now labelled parameter; no two tiers of any ladder share an outcome; the near-misses are all excluded by the rules alone; and the whole-baseline figures 72.00, 304.00, 2116.00 and 3597.01 are definite and wrong.
Draft recomputation from the visible context: performed and recorded above.

AUDIT RESPONSE — round 3, against env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/lodging_reservations_desk/1.md and _difficulty.md. Each item is answered by its own id.
T1-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, a straw-man baseline behind nights_given_up_basis). Closed in two places at once. The factor's baseline is now the expression the baseline paragraph actually states — the nights the reservation covers less the nights the folio shows consumed where a departure is recorded, and none where no departure is recorded — so on this world it is four nights, not zero. And the world no longer masks the difference: the notice tier used to cap the retained nights at the unit type's late cancellation nights, which made three given-up nights and four indistinguishable; it now takes the late cancellation allowance off the nights given up, so three give two retained nights and four give three, and the factor moves the scored figure from 630.12 to 927.69 when its honest baseline is substituted. The whole-baseline figure is now 2116.00, which is exactly the number the audit derived from baseline.rule for a reader who finds the computation document and no factor document.
T1-2 / F-3 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, undeclared override of the housekeeping and parking amounts). Closed by declaring it: lodging_ext_departure_service_charge.overwrite is no longer empty. It names base lodging_rate_and_fees "The housekeeping charge is posted once on departure and the parking charge nightly for spaces beyond those included." verbatim, replaced by a new sentence of the extended rule that makes those two published figures the starting point, varies each by the records and adds the turnover charge on top of the housekeeping charge — one declaration covering all three ladders, since one base sentence fixes both quantities. The dossier's earlier claim that base fixes no figure is struck: base carries cleaning_fee_usd and parking_nightly_usd as its own per-tier parameters, and the paragraph above says so.
T1-3 / F-5 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, the credit ladder states no status while the compute filters one). Closed by putting the state in the prose: the rule now says outright that credit counts only where the record carrying it is itself live — a season pass record standing active for the season, or a ticket order standing in use — and every tier of the ladder names those states, in the same words as the compute's filters. The near-miss still excludes: the 400.00 on the cancelled pass is now out on a sentence the reader can find, not on an unstated filter, and the settlement figure is the one the prose gives.
T1-4 (observation, base's "settled before the party leaves the mountain" inherited and not met). Closed by declaring it rather than leaving it standing: lodging_ext_departure_settlement.overwrite now names that base sentence verbatim and replaces it with a sentence of the extended rule settling a folio the household takes up later on the same basis, which is what this task does six days after the departure.
T1-5 (observation, retained_nightly_rate labelled parameter while tier 1 changes the source of the rate). No change, with the reason recorded in the factor card: all three tiers yield one nightly rate multiplied into the same expression, so no algorithm changes between them and parameter is the honest label. The computation's method factor is nights_given_up_basis, whose tiers select three different counting rules.

Renata Falkowski is a hospital pharmacist from Park City who took a studio at Granite Ridge over the holidays for herself, her husband, her son Jonas and her mother, and the week ended badly: they came home before New Year and she has been on the phone to one office or another ever since. She sounds tired rather than cross, and she talks in long sentences with an apology at the end of them. What she wants is simple and she says it at the start: she would like to close off the folio on that studio, pay whatever is genuinely owed today, and stop thinking about it. She rings from the number the collective has for her, 3035550483, and offers it straight away as the way to find the account.

Anything else about herself comes only when the agent asks for it, one item at a time: she was born on 1971-11-03, her passholder number is GR44025831, her postal code is 84098 and her email is renata.falkowski@cascademail.com. If the agent asks who the booking was in, she says it was in her own name; if asked who was in the unit, she says the four of them, her son included, and the little dog. If asked why the stay ended when it did, she says her mother fell on the second morning and they drove her home on the Wednesday, and that she has a claim in with the protection people about it, which as far as she knows is still being looked at.

She mentions once, without pressing, that she rang yesterday about a charge on the folio she did not understand and was told someone would look at it; she does not know what happens to that charge and does not ask for it to be taken off. She has no idea what the total should be. If the agent asks her what she thinks she owes, she laughs and says she gave up trying to work it out, and that whatever the folio says is what she will pay. She will not offer a figure of her own at any point, and if a figure is put to her she takes it as read.

Only when it comes to paying does she say how she wants it done: not a new card over the phone, but the card the collective already has on file, and she would rather press the button herself than have the desk take it without her. She is content for the agent to put the folio in order first without explaining every line, as long as it is done before she pays. When the agent tells her the amount and hands the payment over to her, she makes it with the reservation reference the agent gives her, the amount the agent states and the card on file, and she takes whatever figure she is given as read.

Once she hears the folio is settled she thanks the agent, says something about being glad it is done, and rings off. If she is told part of it is still with someone else to look at, she accepts that without argument.
